BREAKING: US households now own ~42% of the US equity market, their highest proportion since the late 1990s.

This proportion has risen +7 percentage points since 2020.

Foreign investors are the 2nd-largest owners, accounting for 18%, up from 16% in 2020.

Mutual funds rank 3rd, https://t.co/sbKghpskHX
hits.draft_en:
Everyone calls it a retail frenzy. The ownership data says Main Street simply owns more of the market.

US households now hold ~42% of US equities, the highest since the late 1990s and +7 points since 2020, per The Kobeissi Letter.

That's a bigger wealth effect on the way up, and a bigger one on the way down.
hits.video_tip: Stacked-bar or pie of who owns US stocks (households 42%, foreign 18%), animate the +7 pt rise since 2020; 8-10s.

hits.name: unusual_whales
hits.text:
The average price of gasoline during Trump’s second term has now passed the average under Biden, per Reuters

Gas is averaging $4.29 a gallon, up about 41% from a year ago, and has stayed above $4 for a record 158 days, driven by the Iran war and attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.
hits.draft_en:
Gas has stayed above $4 for a record 158 days, averaging $4.29, up about 41% from a year ago, per Reuters.

That's an energy shock, not a new inflation regime.

Shocks end when supply returns, and when energy rolls over, inflation and rates follow it down.
hits.video_tip: Gas-station price sign close-up, then a simple line of the 158-day streak with the $4 line highlighted; end on 'shock, not regime'. 8s.
